result:
`final.py` (a copy of c10) scores **86.5 on the search split**, against about 1.0 for the baseline. I used **10 of the 24 scorer calls** and about 9 minutes of the default 15-minute budget. It reports exactly the reference's pairs on 300 small edge-case inputs, about 6,000 random inputs built around the 80% boundary, inputs with 500-token records, and my own test seeds that I never tuned on (61× faster than the reference there).

| | search score |
|---|---|
| baseline | ~1.0 |
| first working version (c1) | 70.5 |
| final pick (c10 → `final.py`) | 86.5 (scored twice: 86.56 and 86.45) |

The held-out score is taken later on unseen instances, so I don't have it.

**Why it is faster.** The reference compares every pair of records. The final version:
- **Exact duplicates:** identical word sets are grouped by hashing and paired directly.
- **Size filter:** sets of 3 words or fewer can only match an identical set, so they skip the search. Otherwise only sets with at least 80% as many words are compared.
- **Rare words first:** each set's words are sorted from rarest to most common. Two sets that are 80% alike must share a word among each other's first few rare words, so only those words are indexed and looked up. The exact `5·|A∩B| ≥ 4·|A∪B|` test then runs on that small candidate list.
- **Words in no other record** are skipped in lookups, since they can never match. A record whose first few words are all such words is skipped entirely.

**Other approaches tried:**
- Sorting words alphabetically instead of rarest-first was 7× slower on my test data.
- Indexing by word and set size was slightly slower.
- Dropping the `collections` import (counting words in a plain loop) scored worse twice: 78 and 82.8.
- c12 dropped the per-word size pointer. It tied on the scorer (86.75) but was about 6% slower on my heavier test data, so I kept c10 as the safer pick for unseen inputs.

**Candidate log** (calls left: 14, minutes left: ~6)
| candidate | change | scorer | kept? |
|---|---|---|---|
| c1 | rare-words-first index + size filter + duplicate grouping | 70.5 | parent |
| c2 | numeric word ranks, built-in `Counter` for word counts | 82.0 | parent |
| c3 | index by word and set size | — | dropped (slower locally) |
| c4 | skip too-small sets with `bisect` | 77.4 | dropped |
| c5 | c2 without imports | 78.0 | dropped |
| c6 | alphabetical word order | — | dropped (7× slower) |
| c7 | building the word sets with `map`/`dict(zip)` (C-level) | — | parent |

| c9 | give those words rank −1 and use one sort | 86.4 | parent |

I stopped with about 6 minutes and 14 calls left because the last changes moved the score by less than 1%. The remaining time goes into building word sets, counting words and per-record sorting, and those had no big savings left that I could find.
